papers.title: Learning-based Attitude Estimation with Noisy Measurements and Unknown Gyro Bias
papers.authors: Parham Oveissi; Mohammad Mirtaba; Ankit Goel
papers.why: Gyroscope integration drifts under unknown bias; an SO(3) filter must correct the rotation without breaking its manifold structure.
papers.method: Retrospective Cost Attitude Estimator (RCAE): propagate rotation with the measured angular increment and apply a multiplicative correction tuned by retrospective-cost adaptive control. The correction avoids the MEKF measurement Jacobian and does not explicitly estimate gyro bias.
papers.math: R_{k+1} = R_k exp([omega_m]x Delta t) exp([u_k]x), with the second exponential a data-adaptive correction; note the paper's measured orientation input rather than reducing it to a gravity-only observation.
papers.evidence: Numerical simulations and physical attitude-estimation comparisons with a multiplicative EKF are described in the primary paper. No matched TG-DCM dataset or tilt metric is published.
papers.limits: Crucial task mismatch: the estimator is provided noisy orientation measurements, not only a six-axis acceleration/gyro stream; do not call it a six-axis-only competitive baseline without replacing that measurement channel.
papers.transfer: Consider multiplicative/SO(3) correction or retrospective adaptation as a separately benchmarked filter head; preserve the gravity-only yaw gauge.

papers.title: A robust adaptive error state Kalman filter for MEMS IMU attitude estimation under dynamic acceleration
papers.authors: Xiaofeng Wei; Shiwei Fan; Ya Zhang; Wei Gao; Feng Shen; Xie Ming; Jian Yang
papers.why: Acceleration beyond gravity corrupts roll/pitch correction in conventional inertial attitude filters.
papers.method: Nominal direction-cosine matrix plus small error-state filter; adaptive disturbance handling switches between explicit dynamic-acceleration compensation and measurement-noise covariance adjustment according to monitored motion thresholds.
papers.math: R_true approximately R_nom exp([delta theta]x). The EKF updates a local error state instead of adding nine independent DCM components; dynamic acceleration changes measurement residual reliability.
papers.evidence: Publisher abstract reports at least 42.76% pitch and 67.21% roll improvement in selected dynamic experiments, but these are authors' scenario-specific comparisons, not results on the TG-DCM benchmark.
papers.limits: Full methods and data tables not acquired; threshold sensitivity, motion-distribution shift and covariance-consistency properties remain unverified; no implementation inspected.
papers.transfer: Implement as direct six-axis baseline with identical preprocessing, calibration, per-sequence tilt metrics and time-window latency.

papers.title: EqNIO: Subequivariant Neural Inertial Odometry
papers.authors: Royina Karegoudra Jayanth; Yinshuang Xu; Ziyun Wang; Evangelos Chatzipantazis; Daniel Gehrig; Kostas Daniilidis
papers.why: The same pedestrian motion expressed in different yaw-aligned sensor frames otherwise forces a learned odometry network to memorize redundant directions.
papers.method: Build gravity-aligned equivariant vector and invariant scalar representations; learn an O(2)-subequivariant canonical frame and rotate IMU features into it; regress displacement/covariance in canonical coordinates then transform predictions back.
papers.math: For gravity-preserving Q, mu(QX)=Q mu(X) and Sigma(QX)=Q Sigma(X) Q^T. Under reflections, gyroscope angular velocity is axial rather than polar, requiring the appropriate parity handling.
papers.evidence: Paper evaluates TLIO, Aria, RIDI, OxIOD and a RoNIN-derived model; repository implements vector-neuron network primitives and probabilistic displacement loss. Odometry ATE is not attitude tilt RMSE.
papers.limits: Requires a gravity-aligned reference; the choice of subgroup and canonicalization can hide sensitivity to inaccurate estimated vertical. Its specific O(2) symmetry is not automatically arbitrary SO(3) remount equivariance.
papers.transfer: Derive a causal SO(3)-covariant tilt correction on S^2 without needing an externally supplied attitude estimate; use exact remount tests.

papers.title: DIVE: Deep Inertial-Only Velocity Aided Estimation for Quadrotors
papers.authors: Angad Bajwa; Charles Champagne Cossette; Mohammed Ayman Shalaby; James Richard Forbes
papers.why: A quadrotor can lose camera tracking and pure IMU double integration then produces rapidly diverging navigation estimates.
papers.method: Regress three-axis velocity from causal IMU history and use it as an update in an on-manifold extended Kalman filter.
papers.math: The learned virtual velocity measurement supplies an innovation to a geometric filter; errors in gyro bias still propagate through its nominal attitude and velocity dynamics.
papers.evidence: Authors report 42% better localization on in-distribution flights, 22% OOD and 43% over dead reckoning in a VIO-failure scenario; no matched six-axis tilt benchmark.
papers.limits: Trajectory metrics and flight distribution are different from tilt estimation. Full implementation was not inspected.
papers.transfer: Learned pseudo-measurement integrated into geometric filter, with an explicit measurement noise and testable innovation consistency.

papers.title: On the effects of angular acceleration in orientation estimation using inertial measurement units
papers.authors: Felix Brändle; David Meister; Marc Seidel; Robin Strässer; Frank Allgöwer
papers.why: Low-cost IMU orientation estimation fails during rotational acceleration, even when gravity is predictable at the body origin.
papers.method: Derive transfer functions including accelerometer displacement from a rotation center, then analyze Mahony/Madgwick feedback and nonminimum-phase operating regimes.
papers.math: Rigid-sensor acceleration contains alpha x r + omega x (omega x r). Linearized transfer zeros can enter the right half plane depending on lever arm and operating point; lowering feedback gain trades tracking bandwidth for disturbance attenuation.
papers.evidence: Analytical model, numerical/experimental study of tracking vs bandwidth, with explicit orientation-filter consequences.
papers.limits: Linearization and platform geometry determine when predictions apply; does not provide a general learned attitude estimator or globally optimal filter.
papers.transfer: Include lever-arm-controlled dynamic acceleration and closed-loop bandwidth in evaluation; mere accelerometer norm gating is insufficient.

papers.title: AirIO: Learning Inertial Odometry with Enhanced IMU Feature Observability
papers.why: Rotating IMU acceleration into a gravity/world frame can discard informative body-motion interactions in aerial dynamics.
papers.method: Learn body-frame motion using temporal CNN + recurrent features; compare versions with explicit attitude input, predict velocity and heteroscedastic uncertainty and fuse through an estimator.
papers.math: Rather than collapsing the input to world-frame specific force, body-frame a and omega are retained, and a learned covariance conditions downstream filter updates.
papers.evidence: Authors' ablations and published aerial trajectory results; inspected actual CNNEncoder, CodeNetMotion/CodeNetMotionwithRot and training/evaluation entry points.
papers.limits: An attitude-aided network is not six-axis standalone without explaining how attitude is obtained; reported translation metrics are not tilt metrics, and sensor remounting is not automatically equivariant.
papers.transfer: Compare body-frame temporal context with gravity-aligned processing and uncertainty-conditioned updates; avoid importing an unavailable attitude input.

papers.title: Tartan IMU: A Light Foundation Model for Inertial Positioning in Robotics
papers.why: Models tied to one device, embodiment or dataset generalize poorly to other locomotion and sensor domains.
papers.method: Cross-platform IMU feature pretraining, lightweight ResNet-LSTM trunk and platform-specific output heads with efficient adaptation.
papers.math: The shared sequence encoder maps sensor windows to latent motion representations; per-platform heads predict motion and are fine-tuned instead of retraining all parameters.
papers.evidence: CVPR paper reports multi-platform experiments and adaptation; released Python code contains registered LSTM Foundation_Model but its Transformer builder explicitly raises NotImplementedError because that core was not released.
papers.limits: The public Transformer implementation is not available in the inspected revision; its inertial positioning targets and velocity/trajectory metrics differ from roll/pitch.
papers.transfer: Pretrain a compact causal encoder over heterogeneous IMU devices, evaluate adaptation by held-out device and mount; release exact inference core and checkpoints.

papers.title: iMoT: Inertial Motion Transformer for Inertial Navigation
papers.authors: Son Minh Nguyen; Linh Duy Tran; Duc Viet Le; Paul J. M. Havinga
papers.why: Long-range attention alone may obscure local motion transitions and desynchronized gyro/accelerometer interactions.
papers.method: Transformer with a Progressive Series Decoupler, adaptive positional encoding across inertial modalities, learned query motion particles, and dynamic particle scoring for segment-level velocity.
papers.math: Attention and query-particle aggregation model multiple plausible motions, rather than maintaining only a single deterministic recurrent state.
papers.evidence: AAAI publication evaluated navigation/trajectory accuracy; GitHub publication listing observed but operational model code not verified.
papers.limits: Non-causal/future-window characteristics and computational budget cannot be assumed compatible with instant tilt tracking; trajectory targets only.
papers.transfer: Treat multi-resolution temporal encoders as a controlled ablation; demand lookahead/latency budgets and same sensor channels.

papers.title: Learned IMU Bias Prediction for Invariant Visual Inertial Odometry
papers.authors: Abdullah Altawaitan; Jason Stanley; Sambaran Ghosal; Thai Duong; Nikolay Atanasov
papers.why: Unknown, slowly drifting gyro/accelerometer bias contaminates integration and complicates invariant filter symmetry.
papers.method: Predict IMU bias from historical sensor windows using a learned model, then feed corrected measurements into an invariant MSCKF instead of adding bias as an ordinary group-state component.
papers.math: omega_corr = omega_m - bhat_g(x_history), a_corr = a_m - bhat_a(x_history); geometric propagation remains separate from a learned nuisance-state estimate.
papers.evidence: Real visual-inertial tests include periods of visual outage; does not establish unassisted six-axis gravity-only yaw accuracy.
papers.limits: VIO evaluation assumes images during some segments and a particular filter state/observability structure; bias estimates may entangle motion cues if not regularized.
papers.transfer: Explore slow-time-scale bias state and uncertainty without supervising spurious absolute yaw, with rest, thermal, and time-drift tests.

papers.title: IONext: Unlocking the Next Era of Inertial Odometry
papers.why: Pure Transformers can miss high-frequency local motion detail despite their long-range receptive field.
papers.method: CNN-style Dual-wing Adaptive Dynamic Mixer combines global and local motion features; Spatio-Temporal Gating Unit selects temporally relevant events.
papers.math: Input-conditioned multi-scale mixing and temporal gating act as a selective motion representation, not a physical attitude observer.
papers.evidence: Authors report six inertial navigation datasets and average ATE/RTE improvements over iMoT on an RNIN split; no TG-DCM tilt evidence.
papers.limits: Main task is inertial odometry. Code, matched latency and OOD sensor-mount effects were not verified.
papers.transfer: Test small multi-rate temporal convolutions vs the GRU under fixed parameter count/streaming latency.

papers.title: Effects of Gyroscope Bias Augmentation on Recurrent Neural Network Model Performance for Attitude Estimation
papers.authors: Ji Hoon Park; Chang June Lee; Jung Keun Lee
papers.why: Gyroscope bias sensitivity damages recurrent six-axis attitude estimators and synthetic bias augmentation may be insufficiently characterized.
papers.method: Investigate recurrent model performance when training gyro signals are augmented with bias perturbations. Detailed architecture/protocol unavailable in this review.
papers.math: Synthetic omega_train = omega_measured + b_sample, with b_sample distribution and temporal correlation requiring confirmation against paper methods.
papers.evidence: Publisher DOI and abstract were located; quantitative findings, experiment setup and paper tables were not independently checked.
papers.limits: Do not infer optimal bias distribution, improvement magnitude or model choice without full text.
papers.transfer: Run controlled constant/random-walk/temperature-proxy gyro bias ablations and report separate device OOD performance.

papers.title: A deep learning framework for robust attitude estimation in dynamic environments from six-axis raw inertial measurements
papers.authors: Wei Ding; Yansen Hu; Wei Sun; Zhe Yue
papers.why: Fixed-gain filters and gyro integration perform poorly under dynamic acceleration and raw-sensor distribution shifts.
papers.method: Residual temporal CNN feature extractor joined to bidirectional LSTM context; normalized quaternion output from raw 3-axis accel + 3-axis gyro, with bounded lookahead.
papers.math: The network maps a time window a_{t-w:t+l}, omega_{t-w:t+l} to qhat_t; l>0 incurs algorithmic lookahead and must be accounted for when comparing causal systems.
papers.evidence: Publisher abstract claims median attitude error under 3 degrees and over 10% improvement against selected baselines; lacks same-split TG-DCM comparison or accessible full results here.
papers.limits: Full text inaccessible; detailed loss, dataset splits, runtime and available code not verified. Bidirectionality prohibits treating the output as zero-lookahead without an explicit buffer policy.
papers.transfer: Highest-priority direct modern comparator: reproduce on same six-axis datasets at matched latency and same yaw-invariant tilt RMSE.

papers.title: A Physics-Informed Dual-Branch LSTM Network for UAV Position and Attitude Estimation
papers.authors: Authors as listed in journal DOI
papers.why: Pure regression of UAV position and orientation ignores rigid-body kinematic coupling and drift-inducing physical inconsistency.
papers.method: Shared temporal LSTM encoder with separate position and quaternion attitude branches; kinematic losses include attitude propagation, coordinate transform, velocity-position integration and initial-state constraints.
papers.math: Use quaternion kinematics q_{t+1} approximately q_t tensor Exp(omega_t Delta t / 2) and p_{t+1}=p_t+v_t Delta t, with additional world/body acceleration transformation. Published loss specifics require separate reproduction.
papers.evidence: Open-access full text obtained through scholarly connector; UZH-FPV Drone Racing evaluations, position RMSE 0.0654 m in stated experiment, plus ablations. The paper explicitly assumes dataset-provided initial reference state and neglects explicit online gyro drift compensation.
papers.limits: Absolute position cannot be maintained from an unconstrained six-axis IMU without additional assumptions/prior; short-sequence, initialized evaluation is not a proof of arbitrary-duration drift-free inertial navigation. Position RMSE is not tilt.
papers.transfer: Use branch-specific constrained losses only where auxiliary state variables and reference initialization are available and auditable.

papers.title: MoRPI-PINN: a physics-informed framework for mobile robot pure inertial navigation
papers.why: Pure 2D inertial integration is highly sensitive to noise and gyro/accelerometer bias.
papers.method: Encode 2D inertial navigation differential equations as training residuals alongside data and initial-condition constraints; exploit controlled snake-like robot motion.
papers.math: L = lambda_data L_data + lambda_phys ||d xhat/dt - f_INS(xhat,u)||^2 + lambda_init L_init, with paper-specific term details and scaling to be checked in exact reproduction.
papers.evidence: Real robot study over six trajectories reports position error 4.2m vs 68.6m for 2D INS and 22.1m for MoRPINet, under the study's specific motion setup.
papers.limits: Snake-like motion is a deliberate observability/denoising assumption; no direct evidence of general SO(3) attitude improvement and no public code evaluated here.
papers.transfer: A physically consistent, learnable update is preferable to unconstrained regression when physical state/assumptions are explicitly modeled.

papers.title: AI-IO: An Aerodynamics-Inspired Real-Time Inertial Odometry for Quadrotors
papers.authors: Jiahao Cui; Feng Yu; Linzuo Zhang; Yu Hu; Danping Zou
papers.why: For quadrotors, body velocity may be poorly identified from accelerometer and gyro history without modeling aerodynamic drag and thrust.
papers.method: Combine inertial sensors with rotor speed to make drag/thrust more informative, use CNN features + transformer encoder to predict velocity/uncertainty, fuse with uncertainty-aware EKF.
papers.math: Authors model a_x approximately -lambda_x omega_m^2 v_x - k1 v_x - k2 v_x^2 + bias + noise; using omega_m (motor speed) changes input observability relative to six-axis IMU.
papers.evidence: Authors report 36.9% gain from rotor speed and 22.4% additional gain from architecture in velocity prediction; inspected actual IMUTransformerWithModality and heteroscedastic Gaussian loss.
papers.limits: Not IMU-only in the strict six-axis setting; windless or simplified aerodynamic assumptions and platform-specific rotor information limit transfer.
papers.transfer: Use as justification for declaring observability assumptions and testing conditional side-channel sensing, not as a strict six-axis tilt baseline.

papers.title: KISS-IMU: Self-supervised Inertial Odometry with Motion-balanced Learning and Uncertainty-aware Inference
papers.authors: Jiwon Choi; Hogyun Kim; Geonmo Yang; Juhui Lee; Younggun Cho
papers.why: Collecting exact navigation ground truth across motion types is costly; common slow motions dominate training and rare rapid turns fail.
papers.method: Use LiDAR ICP registration and pose-graph optimization as pseudo-supervision during training; motion feature Gaussian mixtures balance training and adaptive uncertainty weighting governs inference.
papers.math: For motion-component k with empirical density p(k), increase relative weight of underrepresented k subject to clipping; correct the neural integration using uncertainty-based factor weights.
papers.evidence: Authors demonstrate quadruped and other motion datasets; inspected sklearn GaussianMixture implementation, mixture-based weighting, covariance weight controller, and PyPose integrator.
papers.limits: Not sensor-only self-supervision during training: LiDAR supplies the target; teacher ICP failure can bias pseudo-labels. Translational error metrics do not establish tilt improvement.
papers.transfer: Use motion-component balancing and per-motion robustness assessments, with correct group-level split to avoid near-duplicate leakage.

papers.title: GINIO: A Geometric SO(3)-Equivariant Interface for Neural Inertial Odometry
papers.authors: Chankyo Kim; Minghan Zhu; Tzu-Yuan Lin; Avantika Rattan; Maani Ghaffari
papers.why: Rotating or remounting the IMU should transform motion means/covariances predictably; ordinary sensor-frame networks violate the geometric law.
papers.method: SO(3)-equivariant vector-neuron convolution/GRU and geometry-aware outputs; Last-Frame Alignment (LFA) for equivariant models; spectral covariance parameterization transported by congruence.
papers.math: m(QZ)=Qm(Z) and Sigma(QZ)=Q Sigma(Z) Q^T. In vector-neuron GRU, update/reset gates are invariant scalars and hidden features are 3-vectors transformed equivariantly.
papers.evidence: Paper reports TLIO, NanoBench and Fetch remount robustness and ATE (meters); actual repository includes code and an author-side docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md audit documenting several paper-to-checkpoint discrepancies.
papers.limits: Important evidence failures in public erratum: some printed covariance NLL/NEES values lack measured support; an LFA-labeled checkpoint was trained without LFA; a NanoBench comparison mixed TLIO-pretrained and NanoBench-trained models; with-attitude input is not equivariant under certain physical remount transformations; some rotation robustness cells lack generators or reuse different weights. Do NOT present all paper tables as reproduced.
papers.transfer: Evaluate *actual* SO(3) remount transformations including attitude-channel transformation and covariance; demand checkpoint hashes, settings and regeneration scripts for every published cell.

papers.title: Motion-Acceleration Calibration and Compensation in IMUs without External Equipment for Attitude Estimation Filters
papers.why: When IMU is not at the rotation center, tangential and centripetal acceleration contaminate the apparent gravity direction and confidence gating alone discards potentially recoverable information.
papers.method: Calibrate accelerometer/gyro scale, bias, axis misalignment, IMU-to-pivot lever arm and optionally multi-IMU extrinsics from multiposition/static-and-rotation maneuvers; subtract modeled rotational accelerations online.
papers.math: a_sensor = a_origin + alpha x r + omega x (omega x r). Given r and estimates of omega and alpha, remove the last two terms before gravitational tilt correction.
papers.evidence: Primary arXiv HTML contains derivations, simulation and real spherical-mobile-system experiments; authors link open-source code and calibration data at fallow24/ros_imu_calib. This particular code was not inspected.
papers.limits: Needs fixed/known pivot model over calibration motion; differentiating gyro to obtain alpha amplifies noise; cannot remove arbitrary translational acceleration from IMU alone.
papers.transfer: Add calibrated deterministic rotational acceleration compensation ahead of a learned confidence gate, and report the assumptions and failure modes.

papers.title: Self-Supervised Inertial Odometry
papers.authors: Yuheng Qiu; Yutian Chen; Carlton Cort; Weison Huang; Shibo Zhao; Pieter Abbeel; Rocky Duan; Koushil Sreenath; C. Karen Liu; Carmelo Sferrazza; Junyi Geng; Sebastian Scherer; Guanya Shi
papers.why: Each new robot embodiment needs expensive ground-truth trajectory labels before learning a motion prior.
papers.method: Integration self-supervision: a myopic IMU preintegration teacher creates short-window velocity-change targets, a context-rich student denoises them, and pose-graph distillation then produces sequence-consistent targets.
papers.math: Teacher Delta v over a short window is obtained by IMU preintegration; student trained on many windows can average teacher noise under recurrent motion priors, then optimize with graph-consistent pseudo-labels.
papers.evidence: Authors evaluate six datasets and report average velocity error within 0.07 m/s of matched supervised baselines; no dedicated tilt RMSE evidence.
papers.limits: The teacher may inherit gyro/acceleration bias; student gains depend on repeated embodiment dynamics and sufficient excitation. Self-supervision alone cannot create an absolute yaw reference.
papers.transfer: Try physics-generated tilt consistency pseudo-targets only with explicit identifiability analysis and controlled bias/linear-acceleration tests.
